sequences.
#> 315                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          systemPipeR is a workflow management environment for\nreproducible data analysis that integrates R with command-line\nsoftware. It enables researchers to design, execute, and report\ncomplex workflows on local machines and HPC systems. The\nframework combines R-based analysis with external tools through\na Common Workflow Language (CWL) interface, manages workflow\ndependencies and restart capabilities, and automatically\ngenerates reproducible scientific analysis reports. The\ncompanion package systemPipeRdata provides ready-to-use\nworkflow templates that simplify workflow setup and\ncustomization. Alternatively, workflow templates can be loaded\nfrom dedicated GitHub repositories.
#> 316                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             To classify Helicobacter pylori genomes according to\ngenetic distance from nine reference populations. The nine\nreference populations are hpgpAfrica, hpgpAfrica-distant,\nhpgpAfroamerica, hpgpEuroamerica, hpgpMediterranea, hpgpEurope,\nhpgpEurasia, hpgpAsia, and hpgpAklavik86-like. The vertex\npopulations are Africa, Europe and Asia.
#> 317                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     This package implements functions to analyze multi-omics\nepigenetic data. Data of fragment type and base type are\nsupported by epiSeeker. It provides functions to retrieve the\nnearest genes around the peak, annotate genomic region of the\npeak, statistical methods to estimate the significance of\noverlap among peak data sets, and motif analysis. It\nincorporates the GEO database for users to compare their own\ndataset with those deposited in the database. The comparison\ncan be used to infer cooperative regulation and thus can be\nused to generate hypotheses. Several visualization functions\nare implemented to summarize the coverage of the peak\nexperiment, average profile and heatmap of peaks binding to TSS\nregions, genomic annotation, distance to TSS, overlap of peaks\nor genes, and the single-base resolution epigenetic data by\nconsidering the strand, motif, and additional information.
#> 318                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  cogeqc aims to facilitate systematic quality checks on\nstandard comparative genomics analyses to help researchers\ndetect issues and select the most suitable parameters for each\ndata set. cogeqc can be used to asses: i. genome assembly and\nannotation quality with BUSCOs and comparisons of statistics\nwith publicly available genomes on the NCBI; ii. orthogroup\ninference using a protein domain-based approach and; iii.\nsynteny detection using synteny network properties. There are\nalso data visualization functions to explore QC summary\nstatistics.
#> 319                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          A comprehensive package for visualizing multi-set\nintersections and extracting detailed subset information.\nVennDetail generates high-resolution visualizations including\ntraditional Venn diagrams, Venn-pie plots, and UpSet-style\nplots. It provides functions to extract and combine subset\ndetails with user datasets in various formats. The package is\nparticularly useful for bioinformatics applications but can be\nused for any multi-set analysis.
#> 320                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Assorted utilities for multi-modal analyses of single-cell\ndatasets. Includes functions to combine multiple modalities for\ndownstream analysis, perform MNN-based batch correction across\nmultiple modalities, and to compute correlations between assay\nvalues for different modalities.
#> 321                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Wraps common clustering algorithms in an easily extended\nS4 framework. Backends are implemented for hierarchical,\nk-means and graph-based clustering. Several utilities are also\nprovided to compare and evaluate clustering results.
#> 322                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              BatchSVG is a method to identify batch-biased spatially\nvariable genes (SVGs) in spatial transcriptomics data. The\nbatch variable can be defined as sample, donor sex, or other\nbatch effects of interest. The BatchSVG method is based on the\nbinomial deviance model (Townes et al, 2019).
#> 323                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                GOfan provides an intuitive and compact visualization of\nGene Ontology (GO) enrichment results using a sunburst layout\ninspired by SynGO, preserving hierarchical relationships among\nGO terms and allowing color-based encoding of information such\nas p-values or gene counts. By converting complex GO DAGs into\nclean, circular representations, it allows researchers to\nquickly grasp the hierarchical structure and biological\nsignificance of enriched terms. The interactive and\ncustomizable visualizations facilitate exploration of key GO\ncategories, enhancing interpretation and presentation of\nenrichment analyses.
#> 324                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The damidBind package provides a straightforward formal\nanalysis pipeline to analyse and explore differential DamID\nbinding, gene transcription or chromatin accessibility between\ntwo conditions. The package imports processed data from\nDamID-seq experiments, either as external raw files in the form\nof binding bedGraphs and GFF/BED peak calls, or as internal\nlists of GRanges objects. After optionally normalising data,\ncombining peaks across replicates and determining per-replicate\npeak occupancy, the package links bound loci to nearby genes.\nFor RNA Polymerase DamID data, the package calculates occupancy\nover genes, and optionally calcualates the FDR of\nsignificantly-enriched gene occupancy. damidBind then uses\neither limma (for conventional log2 ratio DamID binding data)\nor NOIseq (for counts-based CATaDa chromatin accessibility\ndata) to identify differentially-enriched regions, or\ndifferentially epxressed genes, between two conditions. The\npackage provides a number of visualisation tools (volcano\nplots, Gene Ontology enrichment plots via ClusterProfiler and\nproportional Venn diagrams via BioVenn for downstream data\nexploration and analysis. An powerful, interactive IGV genome\nbrowser interface (powered by Shiny and igvShiny) allows users\nto rapidly and intuitively assess significant\ndifferentially-bound regions in their genomic context.
#> 325                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             GSABenchmark is a package designed for benchmarking\nscRNA-seq gene set analysis (scGSA) methods. It provides both\ntraditional and novel benchmark metrics, as well as\nvisualization tools. Currently, GSABenchmark supports 17 scGSA\nmethods.
#> 326                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          The GENESIS package provides methodology for estimating,\ninferring, and accounting for population and pedigree structure\nin genetic analyses.  The current implementation provides\nfunctions to perform PC-AiR (Conomos et al., 2015, Gen Epi) and\nPC-Relate (Conomos et al., 2016, AJHG). PC-AiR performs a\nPrincipal Components Analysis on genome-wide SNP data for the\ndetection of population structure in a sample that may contain\nknown or cryptic relatedness. Unlike standard PCA, PC-AiR\naccounts for relatedness in the sample to provide accurate\nancestry inference that is not confounded by family structure.\nPC-Relate uses ancestry representative principal components to\nadjust for population structure/ancestry and accurately\nestimate measures of recent genetic relatedness such as kinship\ncoefficients, IBD sharing probabilities, and inbreeding\ncoefficients. Additionally, functions are provided to perform\nefficient variance component estimation and mixed model\nassociation testing for both quantitative and binary\nphenotypes.
#> 327                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Our scLANE model uses truncated power basis spline models\nto build flexible, interpretable models of single cell gene\nexpression over pseudotime or latent time. The modeling\narchitectures currently supported are Negative-binomial GLMs,\nGEEs, & GLMMs. Downstream analysis functionalities include\nmodel comparison, dynamic gene clustering, smoothed counts\ngeneration, gene set enrichment testing, & visualization.
#> 328                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            This package provides functions for creating various\nvisualizations, convenient wrappers, and quality-of-life\nutilities for single cell experiment objects. #> 329                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             Mass spectrometry (MS) data backend supporting import and\nexport of MS/MS spectra data from Mascot Generic Format (mgf)\nfiles. Objects defined in this package are supposed to be used\nwith the Spectra Bioconductor package. This package thus adds\nmgf file support to the Spectra package.
#> 330                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Mass spectrometry (MS) data backend supporting import and\nhandling of MS/MS spectra from NIST MSP Format (msp) files.\nImport of data from files with different MSP *flavours* is\nsupported. Objects from this package add support for MSP files\nto Bioconductor's Spectra package. This package is thus not\nsupposed to be used without the Spectra package that provides a\ncomplete infrastructure for MS data handling.
#> 331                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           scLang is a suite for package development for scRNA-seq\nanalysis. It offers functions that can operate on both Seurat\nand SingleCellExperiment objects. These functions are primarily\naimed to help developers build tools compatible with both types\nof input.
#> 332                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  phyloseq provides a set of classes and tools to facilitate\nthe import, storage, analysis, and graphical display of\nmicrobiome census data.
#> 333                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               A client for BEDbase. bedbaser provides access to the API\nat api.bedbase.org. It also includes convenience functions to\nimport BED files into GRanges objects and BEDsets into\nGRangesLists.
#> 334                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  Battlefield is a Swiss-army toolkit originally developed\nto define and extract spatial spots from specific tissue\nregions—such as front regions, niche borders, invasive margins,\nand cluster interfaces—using spatial transcriptomics data or\nclustered tissue maps. It has since been extended to support\ntrajectory selection and layer inspection, and now provides a\ncollection of low-level utilities for spatial transcriptomics\nanalysis. These utilities are primarily intended to be reused\nwithin higher-level analytical packages. It is designed to work\nwith sequencing-based platforms such as Visium at several\nresolutions and Visium HD(binned).
#> 335                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  MaAsLin2 is comprehensive R package for efficiently\ndetermining multivariable association between clinical metadata\nand microbial meta'omic features. MaAsLin2 relies on general\nlinear models to accommodate most modern epidemiological study\ndesigns, including cross-sectional and longitudinal, and offers\na variety of data exploration, normalization, and\ntransformation methods. MaAsLin2 is the next generation of\nMaAsLin.
#> 336                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Bring the power and flexibility of AnnData to the R\necosystem, allowing you to effortlessly manipulate and analyse\nyour single-cell data. #> 337                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            Test for univariate and bivariate spatial patterns in\nspatial omics data with single-molecule resolution. The tests\nimplemented allow for analysis of nested designs and are\nautomatically calibrated to different biological specimens.\nTests for aggregation, colocalization, gradients and vicinity\nto cell edge or centroid are provided.
#> 338                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       ramr is an R package for detection of epimutations (i.e.,\ninfrequent aberrant DNA methylation events) in large data sets\nobtained by methylation profiling using array or\nhigh-throughput methylation sequencing. In addition, package\nprovides functions to visualize found aberrantly methylated\nregions (AMRs), to generate sets of all possible regions to be\nused as reference sets for enrichment analysis, and to generate\nbiologically relevant test data sets for performance evaluation\nof AMR/DMR search algorithms.
#> 339                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 Provides functionality for untargeted LC-MS metabolomics\nresearch as specified in the associated protocol article in the\n'Metabolomics Data Processing and Data Analysis—Current Best\nPractices' special issue of the Metabolites journal (2020).\nThis includes tabular data preprocessing and quality control,\nuni- and multivariate analysis as well as quality control\nvisualizations, feature-wise visualizations and results\nvisualizations. Raw data preprocessing and functionality\nrelated to biological context, such as pathway analysis, is not\nincluded.
#> 340                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          A shiny interface to the scanMiR package. The application\nenables the scanning of transcripts and custom sequences for\nmiRNA binding sites, the visualization of KdModels and binding\nresults, as well as browsing predicted repression data. In\naddition contains the IndexedFst class for fast indexed reading\nof large GenomicRanges or data.frames, and some utilities for\nfacilitating scans and identifying enriched miRNA-target pairs.
#> 341                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   Extends the Seurat classes and functions to support\nGenomic Data Structure (GDS) files as a DelayedArray backend\nfor data representation. It relies on the implementation of\nGDS-based DelayedMatrix in the SCArray package to represent\nsingle cell RNA-seq data. The common optimized algorithms\nleveraging GDS-based and single cell-specific DelayedMatrix\n(SC_GDSMatrix) are implemented in the SCArray package.\nSCArray.sat introduces a new SCArrayAssay class (derived from\nthe Seurat Assay), which wraps raw counts, normalized\nexpressions and scaled data matrix based on GDS-specific\nDelayedMatrix. It is designed to integrate seamlessly with the\nSeurat package to provide common data analysis in the\nSeuratObject-based workflow. Compared with Seurat, SCArray.sat\nsignificantly reduces the memory usage without downsampling and\ncan be applied to very large datasets.
#> 342                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       IONiseR provides tools for the quality assessment of\nOxford Nanopore MinION data. It extracts summary statistics\nfrom a set of fast5 files and can be used either before or\nafter base calling.  In addition to standard summaries of the\nread-types produced, it provides a number of plots for\nvisualising metrics relative to experiment run time or\nspatially over the surface of a flowcell.
#> 343                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               Provides means to interactively visualize guide RNAs\n(gRNAs) in GuideSet objects via Shiny application. This GUI can\nbe self-contained or as a module within a larger Shiny app. The\ncontent of the app reflects the annotations present in the\npassed GuideSet object, and includes intuitive tools to\nexamine, filter, and export gRNAs, thereby making gRNA design\nmore user-friendly.
#> 344                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               MSstats package provide tools for preprocessing,\nsummarization and differential analysis of mass spectrometry\n(MS) proteomics data. Recently, some MS protocols enable\nacquisition of data sets that result in larger than memory\nquantitative data. MSstats functions are not able to process\nsuch data. MSstatsBig package provides additional converter\nfunctions that enable processing larger than memory data sets.
#> 345                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       The cBioPortalData R package accesses study datasets from\nthe cBio Cancer Genomics Portal. It accesses the data either\nfrom the pre-packaged zip / tar files or from the API interface\nthat was recently implemented by the cBioPortal Data Team. The\npackage can provide data in either tabular format or with\nMultiAssayExperiment object that uses familiar Bioconductor\ndata representations.
#> 346                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              MeLSI (Metric Learning for Statistical Inference) is a\nnovel machine learning method for microbiome data analysis that\nlearns optimal distance metrics to improve statistical power in\ndetecting group differences. Unlike traditional distance\nmetrics (Bray-Curtis, Euclidean, Jaccard), MeLSI adapts to the\nspecific characteristics of your dataset to maximize separation\nbetween groups. The method uses an ensemble of weak learners to\nidentify which microbial features drive group differences,\nproviding both improved statistical power and biological\ninterpretability through feature importance weights.
#> 347                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         SingleMoleculeFootprinting provides functions to analyze\nSingle Molecule Footprinting (SMF) data. Following the workflow\nexemplified in its vignette, the user will be able to perform\nbasic data analysis of SMF data with minimal coding effort.\nStarting from an aligned bam file, we show how to perform\nquality controls over sequencing libraries, extract methylation\ninformation at the single molecule level accounting for the two\npossible kind of SMF experiments (single enzyme or double\nenzyme), classify single molecules based on their patterns of\nmolecular occupancy, plot SMF information at a given genomic\nlocation.
#> 348                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          An R implementation of the correlation-based method\ndeveloped in the Joshi laboratory to analyse and filter\nprocessed single-cell RNAseq data. It returns a filtered\nversion of the data containing only genes expression values\nunaffected by systematic noise.
#> 349                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              seqsetvis enables the visualization and analysis of sets\nof genomic sites in next gen sequencing data. Although\nseqsetvis was designed for the comparison of mulitple ChIP-seq\nsamples, this package is domain-agnostic and allows the\nprocessing of multiple genomic coordinate files (bed-like\nfiles) and signal files (bigwig files pileups from bam file).\nseqsetvis has multiple functions for fetching data from regions\ninto a tidy format for analysis in data.table or tidyverse and\nvisualization via ggplot2.
#> 350                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             SpaceTrooper performs Quality Control analysis using data\ndriven GLM models of Image-Based spatial data, providing\nexploration plots, QC metrics computation, outlier detection.\nIt implements a GLM strategy for the detection of low quality\ncells in imaging-based spatial data (Transcriptomics and\nProteomics). It additionally implements several plots for the\nvisualization of imaging based polygons through the ggplot2\npackage.
#> 351                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          In high resolution mass spectrometry (HR-MS), the measured\nmasses can be decomposed into potential element combinations\n(chemical sum formulas). Where additional mass/intensity\ninformation of respective isotopic peaks is available,\ndecomposition can take this information into account to better\nrank the potential candidate sum formulas. To compare measured\nmass/intensity information with the theoretical distribution of\ncandidate sum formulas, the latter needs to be calculated. This\npackage implements fast algorithms to address both tasks, the\ncalculation of isotopic distributions for arbitrary sum\nformulas (assuming a HR-MS resolution of roughly 30,000), and\nthe ranked list of sum formulas fitting an observed peak or\nisotopic peak set.
#> 352                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               R-package with shiny interface, provides a framework for\nthe analysis of transcriptomics, proteomics and/or metabolomics\ndata. The interface offers a guided experience for the user,\nfrom the definition of the experimental design to the\nintegration of several omics table together. A report can be\ngenerated with all settings and analysis results.
#> 353                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  TreeAndLeaf implements a hybrid layout strategy that\nenhances leaf-level visualization in dendrograms. By\nintegrating force-directed graph and tree layout algorithms, it\nenables projection of multiple layers of information onto\ngraph–tree diagrams.
